items.hook: One and Three Chairs, is a conceptual work by Joseph Kosuth, from 1965.
items.body: An example of conceptual art, the piece consists of a chair, a photograph of the chair, and an enlarged dictionary definition of the word "chair". Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Americans in Greece refers to American citizens who reside, work, study, or have settled in Greece, as well as their descendants.
items.body: The community encompasses a diverse population including expatriates, retirees, digital nomads, academics, students, military personnel, diplomats, and Greek Americans who have returned to their ancestral homeland. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: The Columbia Daily Spectator is the student-run newspaper of both Columbia University and Barnard College.
items.body: Founded in 1877, it is the second-oldest continuously operating college news daily in the nation after The Harvard Crimson, and has been legally independent from the university since 1962. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: The Korean axe murder incident in Panmunjom results in the deaths of two US Army officers.
items.body: The Panmunjom axe murder incident, also known as the Korean axe atrocity incident, was the killing of two United Nations Command officers, Captain Arthur Bonifas and First Lieutenant Mark Barrett, by North Korean soldiers on August 18, 1976, in the Joint Security Area (JSA) in the Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ). One of those things you can't un-know.
